svg.text: Setting up two breadboards for the ESP32
Only some columns are drawn. Old breadboard = upper, new breadboard = lower.
Remove the lower breadboard's top rail strip
Flip the breadboard, slit the adhesive along the strip joint,
then slide the strip off lengthwise (don't pry it up).
Place it in front of the old breadboard
Its row a side (strip removed) butts against the bottom rail strip
of the old breadboard, now called the middle rail. Line up the left ends.
Line up the ESP32 board, don't press yet
VIN pin in column 4 (upper), 3V3 pin in column 4 (lower). It usually fits on
row i (upper) and row b (lower); if not, slide the lower breadboard.
Result: every pin has free holes
Green = free holes connected to the pin in their column.
This module uses row f (upper) and row e (lower).
